title: A scoop with a view.
summary: Rococo in Kennebunk: our longtime ice-cream pilgrimage, with a little Buenos Aires in the story.
search: The journalKennebunk, MaineA family field noteA familiar stop on our Maine visits. Family photograph.A New England field note · Kennebunk, MaineA scoop with a view.Rococo in Kennebunk: our longtime ice-cream pilgrimage, with a little Buenos Aires in the story.Inside the scoop shop. Family photograph.Come alongRococo has been a pilgrimage for us for years. It is one of those places we keep coming back to when we are in this part of Maine: familiar, eagerly anticipated, and still capable of surprising us. The ice cream is delicious. That is reason enough to go, and a very good reason to return.Looking for arrival and access details?The good part of the visitThe place we keep coming back to.Some stops become part of how you know a place. For us, Rococo belongs to this stretch of the Maine coast. We have been making the pilgrimage for a long time, and the pleasure is both in coming back and in seeing what is on the flavor board this time.The combinations are part of the fun. Rococo’s repertoire includes Goat Cheese Blackberry Chambord, Strawberry Basil, and Maple Fig Jalapeño. These are examples of the maker’s creations, rather than a promise of what will be in the case when you visit. There is imagination here, but the reason we return is much simpler: this is delicious ice cream.A scoop can be the whole outing. We do not need to turn every family stop into a bigger production. Sometimes a place you love, something good to eat, and time together are plenty.The good part of the visit. Family photograph.Start with the useful question +Which arrival, facility or part of the day determines whether this visit works for you? Open the official visitor information.Keep the plan your ownMaine, by way of Buenos Aires.There is a personal thread here for me, too: my Argentinian colleagues. Rococo’s Argentine connection gives me another reason to feel attached to this little Maine ritual.As Rococo tells its story, founder Lauren Guptill spent several years living in Argentina. Buenos Aires and its heladerías helped inspire the business she opened in Kennebunkport in 2012. Today, the scoop shop is at 8 Western Avenue in neighboring Kennebunk.I love that a place can be rooted in Maine and carry inspiration from somewhere else. That is part of Rococo’s appeal: curiosity and creativity, in something as immediately enjoyable as a scoop of ice cream.And now there’s another Buenos Aires chapter in our family album: Mom-Mom and Grandpa Steve stopped at Don Julio in Palermo before their Viking cruise, and found another “1954” for the number they’ve photographed on their travels for years. I love this little connection from Buenos Aires back to Maine.Some places become a family ritual, one delicious return at a time.Pictures to take with youA few words for this story.Choose the pictures that are familiar and useful. Find the access notes for your day.Get your bearings before you set out. Wells Beach: an illustrated geographic schematic North is up. Wells Beach faces the Atlantic Ocean, east of Wells Harbor and the marsh. Atlantic Avenue runs along the beach peninsula, reaching the Eastern Shore parking lot at its north end. Mile Road approaches from the west, with the Mile Road parking lot near its eastern end and Casino Square at the end of the road. Webhannet Drive continues south. Four broad place anchors match the access notes beside this map.
